basics.name: Zoha Rakotomalala
basics.label: Software Development Engineer @ Amazon
basics.summary: Studied business, taught myself software engineering, and haven't looked back. Software engineer at Amazon with a business-school background (EDHEC, UC Berkeley Haas, SKKU). Moved from data-analyst internships into software engineering via Dataiku and Amazon. Drawn to complex problems, new technologies, and work that keeps me learning. Experience across backend services (Java, TypeScript), AWS infrastructure-as-code, cloud migrations, A/B experimentation, and AI coding agents in daily engineering work.

work.name: Amazon
work.summary: Xenos / Cross-marketplace pricing, seller-facing team. Services powering automated, margin-neutral pricing for sellers expanding across international Amazon marketplaces. Focus on infrastructure modernization, cloud migrations and AI-assisted engineering.
highlights: Delivered a migration workstream within the 2026 regional-exit program for pricing services: 4 backend services moved off a legacy AWS region and one legacy data-warehouse cluster deprecated, cutting the region footprint 82% and infrastructure run-rate by about $48K/year, one month ahead of target
Re-platformed fee computation onto a new centralized fee engine and built reusable cross-region networking constructs (AWS CDK), reducing later migrations to configuration changes

Ran backend migrations with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Kiro, internal agents), feeding earlier migrations back in as context so the agents improve with each one, cutting per-migration effort about 26%
Introduced GenAI tooling and MCP-based workflows to 40+ engineers through talks and hands-on sessions, with about 27 hours of engineering effort saved
Built and published an AI agent on Amazon's internal agent registry that drafts career documents grounded in an engineer's real work history; human-in-the-loop by design, it never submits on its own
Recurring hands-on knowledge-sharing sessions for the org, including a session on cross-region networking patterns
On-call for production pricing systems

work.name: Amazon
work.summary: Price Perception, customer-facing team. Fullstack development (Java, TypeScript, internal Amazon stacks) on price transparency and legal-compliance features (price history, price tracker, EU Omnibus directive) for European marketplaces.
highlights: Contributed to the expansion of the EU Omnibus directive compliance feature to Spain and Ireland, launched through A/B experiments to measure customer impact
Authored the Correction of Error after a legal-compliance incident during the Spain launch: root-cause analysis across interconnected systems, mitigation items driven to resolution
Designed the architecture for a new price history customer experience, weighing real-time computation against pre-computed approaches for latency and scalability
Enabled 8 marketplace expansions of the Price Tracker feature (JP, CA, AE, IN, MX, ES, IE, IT): configuration and deployment coordination
Redesigned a core UI component of the price tracker to be scalable and reusable across marketplaces and languages
Identified and documented latency regression correction opportunities in the price tracker service
Coordinated across three engineering teams and senior stakeholders to align technical standards and surface experiment overlap, leading to project consolidation
Presented at an internal Amazon conference on Model Context Protocol (MCP) and its architectural implications for AI-integrated systems
Supervised a software engineering intern for 5 months: technical mentorship, design reviews, guidance on an internal operations dashboard
Team happiness champion: owned the cycle of team feedback surveys, analysis and action-item follow-through
Resolved 15+ production incidents during on-call shifts, none self-caused

Generated graph templates in Java and rendered them through Graphviz

Post-processed the SVG in Angular/TypeScript: mass import of tables, expand/collapse of relation degrees, external table preview, zoom/pan navigation, tooltips, clustering into schema zones, state persistence across modal sessions, connected-column highlighting

Analysed sales and trial engagement touchpoints to explain month-over-month performance variations
Built a data model tracking the daily evolution of customers in trial
Built a model predicting user retention to guide the sales team
Owned QA of several data models, cross-checking Salesforce against back-office data and proposing matching improvements
